cd ~/Desktop/pi-lens && gh issue create --title "turn-end test failures render model-facing framing in the terminal entry, and the in-process model never receives them (refs #2366, #2367)" --label bug --label "area:observability" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Symptom (user report, dogfood session, 2026-09-08)

At turn end the terminal showed, as a pi-lens entry:

```
pi-lens test failures
[pi-lens automated check — not a user request] [from a prior turn — the edit that triggered this run had already been superseded by the time results came back]

[Tests] ✗ 5/19 failed, 14 passed (0.05s) — vitest
  ✗ builds a native provider with auth, getModels, refreshModels, streams
    AssertionError: expected [ { id: 'default', …(10) }, …(2) ] to deeply equal []
  … (5 cases)
  → Fix failing tests before proceeding
```

The user's expectation: "this should only be visible inline to the model".

## What the code does today

- `clients/test-runner-delivery.ts` (PR #2367 for #2366, 2026-08-29) delivers turn-end test failures as a NON-CONTEXT custom entry (`pilens:test-runner-findings`, `appendEntry` + `registerEntryRenderer`) once `agent_settled` proves the agent idle. Custom entries are ignored by `sessionEntryToContextMessages`, so the model never sees them.
- #2366's required contract explicitly says: "Stop consuming `test-runner-findings` for automatic model-context delivery" and "never fall back to `sendMessage`". Grep confirms: `index.ts` no longer builds a `test-findings` context slice; `consumeTestFindings` (`clients/runtime-context.ts:243`) is reached only from the MCP `turn_end` tool (`clients/mcp/session.ts:341`), i.e. an explicit model request, and `lens_diagnostics` pull.
- The entry content is built for a MODEL reader: `AUTOMATION_FRAMING` (`[pi-lens automated check — not a user request]`, `clients/runtime-context.ts:13`), the stale prefix `[from a prior turn — …]` (`clients/runtime-turn.ts:2833`), and the imperative `→ Fix failing tests before proceeding`. `renderTestRunnerEntry` (`clients/test-runner-delivery.ts`) prints that string verbatim under a "pi-lens test failures" header.

So two defects, independent of which direction is chosen:

1. **Framing leak.** Model-directed framing strings are rendered to the human. Whatever the delivery surface, the human-facing render must strip `AUTOMATION_FRAMING`, the stale prefix, and the "fix before proceeding" imperative, or the entry must not be human-facing at all.
2. **Stale delivery to a human.** The `stale` flag was designed so the MODEL can discount a superseded run. Showing a stale batch to the human as a red "test failures" panel is noise (the sample above is exactly that: the edit had been superseded).

## Decision needed (maintainer)

#2366 deliberately moved delivery OUT of model context and INTO the terminal. The report asks for the opposite: model-only, inline. Options:

- **A. Reverse #2366's surface**: deliver at the next safe idle boundary as model context (the pre-#2367 `test-findings` slice, gated by the same staleness/provenance store and the `agent_settled` idle proof), and stop rendering a human entry. #2366's concern was steering the LIVE model mid-run; delivering at the next user prompt's context build does not steer a live run.
- **B. Keep the human entry, fix the leak**: strip model framing in `renderTestRunnerEntry`, suppress stale batches from the human surface, and ALSO restore a model-context delivery so the model acts on failures (today it does not, in-process).
- **C. Both surfaces, split content**: one human-readable summary line in the TUI, full model-facing content in context.

Acceptance to be fixed once the direction is chosen; either way: a regression test that renders the entry (or builds the context) from a stale + framed record and asserts what each audience sees.

Refs #2366 (open), #2367, #2522 (runner-error framing), #2532.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

cd ~/Desktop/plegma && gh issue create -R apmantza/plegma --title "codex + worktree workspace: the default workspace-write sandbox makes the shared .git read-only and cuts network, so a worker can never branch, commit, push, or use the gh passthrough" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened (consumer report, 2026-09-07, four `codex/openai/gpt-5.6-luna` workers, orchestrator = Claude Code via the MCP bridge)

Delegated with `workspace: {mode: "worktree", path: "/home/akis/Desktop/pi-lens"}`, `passthrough: ["gh"]`, `approvals: "auto"`, and a task that granted Git authority (branch, one commit, push, `gh pr create`). All four workers stopped at the same two walls:

```
fatal: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/fix/2721-analyzer-disable-keys':
  Unable to create '/home/akis/Desktop/pi-lens/.git/refs/heads/fix/2721-analyzer-disable-keys.lock': Read-only file system
```

and `gh issue view` / direct GitHub API: unreachable (no network in the sandbox), so the `gh` passthrough that was explicitly granted could not be exercised at all.

Cause: `codex exec` runs with `-s workspace-write` by default on Linux (`resolveCodexSandbox` in `src/backends/codex.ts`). A plegma worktree is `git worktree add`-ed from the source repo, so its `.git` is a pointer file to `<sourceRepo>/.git/worktrees/<handle>` and every ref/index/object write goes to the source repo's common dir — outside the writable root. Network is off in that sandbox mode too. One worker gave up before editing (`done / completed` with zero changes); three kept implementing and will hand back uncommitted trees, so the orchestrator has to do the commit/push/PR from outside — workable, but it silently downgrades the delegation contract and nobody is told at spawn time.

## Asks

1. **Worktree mode should make the git common dir writable.** When the workspace is a worktree, pass codex `-c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<gitCommonDir>"]'` (resolve it with `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` at bind time), or at minimum the `.git/worktrees/<handle>` admin dir plus `refs/`, `objects/`, `index` needs of the common dir. Without it the worktree mode is a read-only checkout for codex.
2. **Network follows `passthrough: ["gh"]`.** Granting the gh credentials while the sandbox has no network is a contradiction; when `passthrough` contains `gh`, set `-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` (or refuse the grant at submit with a readable reason).
3. **Expose `sandbox` per delegation.** `SpawnOptions.sandbox` already exists in the backend but `plegma_delegate` / `plegma_spawn` / the CLI do not take it, and the daemon-level default is startup-only config (same shape as #310). A caller that knows the tree is disposable should be able to ask for `danger-full-access` on one delegation.
4. **Say so in the receipt / early settlement.** A worker that cannot write refs in a worktree workspace with Git authority in its task is going to fail the contract; a `warnings: ["git-common-dir read-only under workspace-write"]` on the receipt (the #190 `warnings` slot already exists) would let the orchestrator adapt before the turn is spent.

## Evidence

- Handles: `sub-mtrpwlmb-2` (bailed, zero edits), `sub-mtrpwve1-3`, `sub-mtrpxah2-4`, `sub-mtrpxr8l-5` (continued without Git). Delegations `dlg-3e712bcf-…`, `dlg-43c20c7d-…`, `dlg-21ef735b-…`, `dlg-3ac7ac0a-…`.
- `plegma tail <handle>` on each shows the "read-only" line above; the `commandcode` worker in the same fleet (`sub-ded8ao`) does not hit it.
- Related: #271 (gh passthrough inconsistent for lunas) is probably this same sandbox network cut, not a credential copy problem.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

cd ~/Desktop/plegma && gh issue create -R apmantza/plegma --title "commandcode: a delegated worker can land in a permission-gated print mode where every mutating tool is denied — approvals:auto does not apply, the turn 'completes' with zero edits" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened (2026-09-08, pi-lens PR #2734 fix round, `commandcode/commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, delegation `dlg-061c4598-6053-4936-9bc4-6d8a7028414f`, handle `sub-05ohcl`)

Delegated with `approvals: "auto"`, `passthrough: ["gh"]`, worktree workspace. The worker reported:

> Every mutating tool in this session — `shell_command`, `edit_file`, `write_file` (including the scratchpad) — is permission-blocked (print mode without `--yolo`). The session is strictly read-only, so I cannot apply the edits, run vitest, commit, push, or call `gh`.

It then settled `done / completed` with a complete edit set in prose and no file changed. Earlier commandcode workers in the same fleet had a partial version of the same thing and worked around it: the #2710 fixer (`sub-ded8ao`) and both GLM reviewers reported "my main session ran print-mode permission-gated (no shell/writes), so one serialized subagent executed the commands" — i.e. they only got work done by spawning an inner subagent that was NOT gated.
